title: Finding Delta for a Quadratic Limit
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find a suitable delta > 0 to prove lim_{x -> 2} x^2 = 4 for an arbitrary epsilon > 0.

steps.title: Factor the Distance |f(x) - L|
steps.explanation: Factor the difference of squares to separate the controllable factor |x - 2|.
steps.why: We can control |x - 2| directly via delta, but need to bound the auxiliary factor |x + 2|.

steps.title: Assume a Prelimimary Bound on Delta
steps.explanation: Constrain delta <= 1 so that x stays within (1, 3), bounding |x + 2| strictly by 5.
steps.why: Imposing an initial constraint on delta establishes a uniform upper bound on non-linear factors.

steps.title: Determine the Final Value of Delta
steps.explanation: Set 5*delta <= epsilon, giving delta <= epsilon/5. Take the minimum of 1 and epsilon/5.
steps.why: Taking the minimum ensures both the preliminary bound |x+2| < 5 and 5|x-2| < epsilon hold.
